content_of_post_to_comment: Recently, I started thinking about how games should reward players for skillful playing. The idea is mostly absent in modern games but it used to be very common in platformers and other arcady games in the early 90s. Ironically, the most common way to reward players for playing well was by making the game easier. This could be done via extra lifes, continues, or power-ups. Obviously, skilled players don’t need these. For example, Sonic 3 and Knuckles is a game I know like the back of my hand. When I finish a playthrough, I have dozens of lifes and continues that I don’t need and I can turn into hyper Sonic to make the game super easy. So, I don’t think this reward system works very well. Instead, I think it would make more sense to reward good players by giving them more content. Sonic 3 & Knuckles has this as we can only access the real final zone if we collected all chaos emeralds. Do you know any game that uses such a reward system? Do you think it’s a good idea in the first place? Should modern games have rewards for skillful playing? Let me know in the comments.
comment: Maybe the better reward isn't more power but more complexity: skilled players could unlock alternate rulesets or constraints, turning mastery into a new way to experience the same world.
